history: user: My home internet's been really sluggish lately. | assistant: I've checked, and your line itself looks healthy right now. When do you notice it most?
question: Mostly at night, like every day after nine, why does it get slower then?
expected_answer: Evenings are peak hours: many more people are streaming and gaming, so shared parts of the network and the sites' servers get congested, and neighbours' Wi-Fi adds interference; a wired speed test helps separate network congestion from Wi-Fi problems.

history: user: The Wi-Fi works fine in the living room where the router is. | assistant: Good, that means the connection itself is healthy. Where does it give you trouble?
question: Upstairs in the bedroom, so do I need to use the two point four network there?
expected_answer: Probably yes: the 2.4 GHz band reaches further and passes through walls and floors better, while 5 GHz is faster but has a shorter range, so upstairs the 2.4 GHz network will usually hold a steadier connection.

question: I'm off to Bali next month, how do I stop apps racking up roaming charges?

question: Can I avoid extra fees abroad by paying in pounds instead of the local currency?
expected_answer: No, pay in the local currency; choosing pounds lets the shop or cash machine provider convert it for you (dynamic currency conversion), usually at a worse exchange rate.

question: Is there a legal reason I need a selfie and photo ID to open an account?
expected_answer: Yes: banks are legally required under anti-money-laundering and know-your-customer rules to verify who you are; the selfie confirms the photo ID belongs to the person applying, which stops impersonation and fraud.

A seasonal changeover when your other set is already mounted on wheels costs $69, including a tire pressure monitor reset. ... If the tires have to be dismounted and mounted on one set of wheels, it costs $139 including balancing.
